boundary: Edge of the debris channel: the Lende Khola / Bhote Koshi valley floor that the 26 Aug 2026 debris flow filled (traced from Sentinel-2 into arrival.bin, drawn ~160 m wider than the true channel) versus the terraces and ridges above it. Settlements on the valley floor (Rasuwagadhi, Ghattekhola, Timure, Syabrubesi bazaar) were buried or swept away; settlements well above the river (Dhunche, upper Syabrubesi) were not. Onlinekhabar reports that the flood reached settlements up to ~80 m (270 ft) above river level.

items.title: Syabrubesi from the air: the town on the terrace stands, the valley floor below it is grey debris
items.place: Syabrubesi (Syaphru Besi) bazaar, riverside main street (Hotel Sky / Small Star Hotel / Hotel New Yalapeak row), Gosaikunda RM, Rasuwa
items.what_it_shows: Single-frame across-the-boundary shot. A thick, flat sheet of grey debris fills the valley floor and is cut by a new river channel with a fresh scarp several metres high. Directly above its edge, multi-storey houses, hotels and terraced fields on the hillside are intact. A few buildings stand right at the debris margin.
items.notes: The town is identified by the caption ('Aerial view of the flood ravaged Syabrubesi'). The lat/lon is the OSM position of the riverside hotel strip, which the article says was 'largely devastated'. I did not pin down the photo's exact viewpoint and orientation. Higher-res versions of the same view, plus an upstream view of the debris-filled valley: https://www.onlinekhabar.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/syaphrubesi-rasuwa-flood.jpg and ...-flood-3.jpg. Pre-event Commons comparators (CC BY-SA 4.0): https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Settlements_at_Syabrubesi,_Langtang.JPG (2013) and https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Syaphru,_Rasuwa.jpg (2008, CC BY-SA 3.0, Krish Dulal, GPS 28.16746 85.33806).

items.title: Upper Syabrubesi: houses on the terrace above the debris line survived
items.place: Upper / new Syabrubesi on the terrace east of the bazaar (Police Post Syapru Besi, Community Bakery, View Point Resort), Gosaikunda RM, Rasuwa
items.what_it_shows: The same aerial photo as the bazaar item: dozens of intact houses and hotels on the terraces just above the debris sheet.
items.notes: The location is approximate: the OSM cluster of upper-town buildings. I could not confirm from the photo which way it faces, so this is the likeliest match for the intact hillside houses in the frame, not a verified one. Use it as the 'unaffected' half of a single-photo pair. For a hero-scale pair, use Dhunche below. Mismatch with NISAR: the hero marks this point as channel because of the 2-pixel widening in export_events.debris_trace.

items.title: Timure: 'only six damaged houses remain standing'
items.place: Timure, Gosaikunda RM-2, Rasuwa (border trade and customs settlement on the Bhote Koshi, ~3 km below Rasuwagadhi)
items.what_it_shows: Kathmandu Post lead photo of Timure after the flood. The article reports that more than 250 houses and structures between Timure and Rasuwagadhi were swept away, including hotels, shops, the customs office, government buildings, and Army, Police and APF checkpoints. 'Only six damaged houses remain standing in Timure.' 125 bodies had been recovered from Timure by mid-September, and 25 students and 6 teachers of Nepal Rastriya Basic School were among the missing.
items.notes: Location from OSM (place=suburb 'टिमुरे'). The same reporter wrote that in the July 2025 flood 'Timure, built on a small rise, escaped the worst' (https://kathmandupost.com/national/2026/09/06/reporter-s-diary-i-went-back-to-rasuwa-the-river-had-changed-everything). That is a good story beat: the rise that saved Timure in 2025 was overtopped in 2026.

items.title: CCTV: the flood hits Gyirong Port at the border crossing
items.place: Gyirong Port / Rasuwagadhi border crossing at the Lende Khola–Bhote Koshi (Kerung Tsangpo) confluence, Nepal–China border
items.what_it_shows: Chinese surveillance-camera frame, 26 Aug 2026 10:59 BJT (~7 min after the collapse signal), looking upstream (NW). A wall of muddy water and debris is destroying the back of the port compound. The port and the Nepali Rasuwagadhi customs office were destroyed, along with 300+ queued vehicles and 400+ containers (Wikipedia).
items.credit: CCTV footage, unknown author, via Wikimedia Commons
items.notes: The point is the OSM 'Rasuwagadhi' hamlet. The port compound is within a few hundred metres, across the border bridge, but the camera position is not given. Video version: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Mudslide_at_Gyirong_Port_1.webm. Pre-event Commons view of the same confluence: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:River_in_Rasuwa.JPG (Krish Dulal, CC BY-SA 3.0, 2013, GPS 28.27835 85.37811).

items.title: Ghattekhola: settlement, immigration office and Rasuwagadhi hydro site 'disappeared'
items.place: Ghattekhola, Gosaikunda RM-2, ~1.5 km below Rasuwagadhi on the Bhote Koshi
items.what_it_shows: Story only (no photo found). Kathmandu Post: Ghattekhola had about 30 houses, the immigration office, the Rasuwagadhi Hydropower Project and six hotels. 'The floods swept them all away, leaving little more than a riverbed of debris.' 12 bodies recovered.
items.notes: This position is my estimate: 1.5 km down-valley from Rasuwagadhi along the river, interpolated between the OSM Rasuwagadhi and Timure points. I could not geocode Ghattekhola itself. Verify before pinning.

items.title: NH42 Trishuli Corridor road and suspension bridge between Syabrubesi and Timure (before)
items.place: NH42 (Pasang Lhamu / Trishuli Corridor road) towards Syaphru, Bhote Koshi valley ~6 km north of Syabrubesi
items.what_it_shows: Pre-event (Nov 2024) ground photo of the valley-floor road and Trishuli suspension bridge. Wikipedia reports that the Syafrubesi–Rasuwagadhi road (NH42) was further damaged and that 33 suspension bridges were damaged beyond repair. Useful as the 'before' for the channel: this valley floor is what the debris filled.
items.notes: Camera GPS comes from the Commons file. The photo predates the event, and I have no post-event photo of this specific bridge, so this item is a 'before' illustration, not proof of damage at this spot.

items.title: Dhunche, the district HQ on the ridge, stayed out of the flood's path and became the access point
items.place: Dhunche bazaar, Gosaikunda RM-6, Rasuwa district headquarters (~2,000 m, ~430 m above the Trishuli)
items.what_it_shows: Pre-event Commons photo of Dhunche's main street. Post-event status from Hiking Nepal (6 Sep 2026): 'Dhunche sits higher above the river and short of the worst-hit stretch of the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli corridor.' The Gosaikunda trail from it 'was not in the flood's path', and limited road access Kathmandu–Dhunche resumed for small vehicles while everything beyond Dhunche towards Syabrubesi and Timure stayed cut off.
items.credit: Photo: Rajivkilanashrestha / Wikimedia Commons (2016). Status: Hiking Nepal, 'Rasuwa Flooding Update', 6 Sep 2026
items.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (photo); story text news, link only
items.notes: Caveats: (1) the photo is pre-event, and I found no post-event photo of intact Dhunche; (2) the source is a trekking company's update, not an agency; (3) Onlinekhabar (26 Aug) lists 'Dhunche' among places where destruction was visible. That probably means riverside parts of the Dhunche area or ward on the Trishuli below the town, not the ridge-top bazaar, but treat it as a conflict to resolve. Other Commons views: File:Dhunche-2019.jpg (Tibetissimo, CC BY-SA 4.0), File:Dhunche_after_rain_-_panoramio.jpg (GPS 28.11024 85.30054).
